overview: Both let a plant skip normal sexual steps, but apomixis produces seeds without fertilisation while parthenocarpy produces fruit without it.
genZNote: Apomixis: seeds made the easy way, no fertilisation needed. Parthenocarpy: fruit forms, but skips making seeds altogether.

aspects.label: What Forms Without Fertilisation
aspects.valueA: Seeds form asexually, genetically identical to the parent plant.
aspects.valueB: Fruit develops without fertilisation, typically resulting in seedless fruit.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Seen in some Citrus and Mango varieties as a form of natural cloning.
aspects.valueB: Seedless varieties like bananas and some grapes.

aspects.label: Commercial Importance
aspects.valueA: Useful in plant breeding to fix hybrid vigour across generations without losing traits.
aspects.valueB: Used to commercially produce seedless fruits, often triggered using growth hormones like auxin or gibberellin.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Apomixis is of major interest to plant breeders because it can lock in hybrid vigour (heterosis) in seeds, generation after generation, without cross-pollination.
overlay.memoryTrick: Apomixis = asexual seeds. Parthenocarpy = 'virgin fruit', fruit without fertilisation.
overlay.commonMisconception: Parthenocarpic fruit isn't necessarily from an apomictic plant — seedless bananas, for example, arise from parthenocarpy, not apomixis.
